  transition: background 0.4s, border-color 0.4s;
}
.s16-box-icon { font-size:28px; flex-shrink:0; }
.s16-box-title { font-size:17px; font-weight:700; text-transform:uppercase; letter-spacing:0.06em; margin-bottom:4px; }
.s16-box-body { font-size:19px; line-height:1.4; }
.s16-box-policy { background:var(--navy); color:#fff; }
.s16-box-policy .s16-box-title { color:rgba(255,255,255,0.4); }
.s16-box-model { background:#fff; border:2px solid var(--border); }
.s16-box-model .s16-box-title { color:var(--muted); }
.s16-box-result { background:#fff; border:2px solid var(--border); }
.s16-box-result .s16-box-title { color:var(--muted); }
.s16-arrow { text-align:center; font-size:28px; color:var(--muted); padding:4px 0; }
.s16-verdict {
  margin-top:12px; border-radius:12px; padding:14px 20px;
  font-size:20px; font-weight:700; text-align:center;
  transition: all 0.4s;
}
.s16-verdict.wrong { background:var(--coral-lt); color:var(--coral-dk); border:2px solid var(--coral); }
.s16-verdict.ok    { background:var(--forest-lt); color:var(--forest); border:2px solid var(--forest); }
.s16-verdict.neutral { background:var(--slate-lt); color:var(--slate); border:2px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.1); }

/* ─── SLIDE 17 — LOGSUM INTERACTIVE ─── */
.s17 {
  display:grid; grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr; gap:48px;
  padding:52px 90px; background:var(--off-white);
}
.s17-eyebrow {
  font-size:17px; font-weight:700; letter-spacing:0.12em;
  text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--forest); margin-bottom:8px;
}
.s17-title {
  font-size:52px; font-weight:700; line-height:1.1;
  color:var(--navy); margin-bottom:16px;
}
.s17-formula-block {
  background:var(--forest-dk); border-radius:14px; padding:20px 24px; margin-bottom:18px;
}
.s17-formula-label { font-size:14px; color:rgba(255,255,255,0.4); text-transform:uppercase; letter-spacing:0.08em; margin-bottom:8px; }
.s17-formula {
  font-size:20px; color:#7ecba1; font-family:var(--mono);
  margin-bottom:6px; line-height:1.4;
}
.s17-formula sub { font-size:0.7em; }
.s17-formula-sub { font-size:17px; color:rgba(255,255,255,0.5); margin-bottom:6px; font-family:var(--mono); }
.s17-formula-note { font-size:16px; color:rgba(255,255,255,0.35); font-style:italic; }
.s17-insights { display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:12px; }
.s17-insight {
  display:flex; gap:14px; align-items:flex-start;
  background:#fff; border-radius:10px; padding:14px 18px;
  box-shadow:0 1px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.05);
}
.s17-insight-num {
  width:28px; height:28px; border-radius:50%;
  background:var(--forest); color:#fff;
  font-size:15px; font-weight:800;
  display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; flex-shrink:0;
}
.s17-insight { font-size:18px; line-height:1.5; color:var(--slate); }
.s17-insight strong { color:var(--navy); }
.s17-right { display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:16px; }
.s17-demo {
  background:#fff; border-radius:16px; padding:24px 28px;
  box-shadow:0 2px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.07); flex:1;
}
.s17-demo-title { font-size:22px; font-weight:700; color:var(--navy); margin-bottom:4px; }
.s17-demo-sub { font-size:16px; color:var(--muted); margin-bottom:16px; }
.s17-demo-inputs { display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:10px; margin-bottom:16px; }
.s17-inp-row {
  display:grid; grid-template-columns:1fr 130px 44px;
  align-items:center; gap:10px;
}
.s17-inp-row label { font-size:16px; font-weight:600; color:var(--slate); }
.s17-inp-row input[type=range] { accent-color:var(--forest); cursor:pointer; }
.s17-inp-row span { font-size:16px; font-weight:700; font-family:var(--mono); color:var(--forest); text-align:right; }
.s17-toll-row label { color:var(--coral); }
.s17-toll-row input[type=range] { accent-color:var(--coral); }
.s17-toll-row span { color:var(--coral); }
.s17-results {
  display:grid; grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr 1fr; gap:8px; margin-bottom:12px;
}
.s17-result-item {
  background:var(--slate-lt); border-radius:8px; padding:10px 14px; text-align:center;
}
.s17-result-item.s17-result-logsum { background:var(--forest-lt); border:2px solid var(--forest); }
.s17-result-label { font-size:14px; font-weight:700; color:var(--muted); margin-bottom:4px; }
.s17-result-label sub { font-size:0.8em; }
.s17-result-val { font-size:20px; font-weight:700; font-family:var(--mono); color:var(--navy); }
.s17-result-logsum .s17-result-val { color:var(--forest); }
.s17-interpretation {
  font-size:16px; line-height:1.5; color:var(--slate);
  background:var(--slate-lt); border-radius:8px; padding:10px 14px;
  min-height:44px; transition:all 0.3s;
}
.s17-strategies { display:grid; grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr; gap:12px; }
.s17-strategy { border-radius:12px; padding:16px 20px; }
.s17-strat-a { background:var(--forest-lt); border:1px solid rgba(29,92,62,0.2); }
.s17-strat-b { background:var(--gold-lt); border:1px solid rgba(201,147,10,0.2); }
.s17-strat-head { font-size:17px; font-weight:700; color:var(--navy); margin-bottom:6px; }
.s17-strat-a .s17-strat-head { color:var(--forest-dk); }
.s17-strat-b .s17-strat-head { color:var(--gold); }
.s17-strategy p { font-size:15px; line-height:1.5; color:var(--muted); }

/* ─── SLIDE 18 — HONEST TRADEOFFS ─── */
.s18 {
  display:flex; flex-direction:column;
  padding:48px 100px; background:var(--off-white);
}
.s18-eyebrow {
  font-size:17px; font-weight:700; letter-spacing:0.12em;
  text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--muted); margin-bottom:6px;
}
.s18-title {
  font-size:50px; font-weight:700; line-height:1.1;
  color:var(--navy); margin-bottom:20px;
}
.s18-cols { display:grid; grid-template-columns:1fr 2px 1fr; gap:28px; flex:1; }
.s18-col { display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:12px; }
.s18-col-head { font-size:20px; font-weight:800; text-transform:uppercase; letter-spacing:0.08em; margin-bottom:4px; }
.pros-head { color:var(--forest); }
.cons-head { color:var(--coral); }
.s18-divider { background:var(--border); }
.s18-pro-item, .s18-con-item {
  display:flex; gap:12px; align-items:flex-start;
  border-radius:10px; padding:12px 16px;
}
.s18-pro-item { background:var(--forest-lt); }
.s18-con-item { background:var(--coral-lt); }
.s18-con-item.s18-highlight {
  background:rgba(232,80,58,0.12); border:1.5px solid var(--coral);
}
.s18-pi-icon, .s18-ci-icon { font-size:22px; flex-shrink:0; margin-top:1px; }
.s18-pi-title { font-size:17px; font-weight:700; color:var(--forest-dk); margin-bottom:3px; }
.s18-ci-title { font-size:17px; font-weight:700; color:var(--coral-dk); margin-bottom:3px; }
.s18-highlight .s18-ci-title { font-size:18px; }
.s18-pro-item p, .s18-con-item p { font-size:16px; line-height:1.45; color:var(--slate); }
.s18-verdict {
  margin-top:16px; text-align:center; font-size:22px; font-weight:700;
  color:var(--navy); background:linear-gradient(135deg, var(--forest-lt), var(--gold-lt));
  border-radius:12px; padding:14px 28px;
}

/* ─── SLIDE 19 — UPDATED TAKEAWAYS ─── */
.s19 {
  background:var(--navy); color:#fff;
  display:flex; flex-direction:column; padding:72px 120px;
  position:relative; overflow:hidden;
}
.s19::after {
  content:''; position:absolute; right:-100px; bottom:-100px;
  width:500px; height:500px; border-radius:50%;
  background:radial-gradient(circle, oklch(0.55 0.12 72/0.25) 0%, transparent 70%);
  pointer-events:none;
}
.s19 .eyebrow { color:var(--amber); }
.s19 .slide-title { margin-bottom:36px; }
.s19 .takeaways { gap:16px; }
.s19 .ta-item { padding:22px 28px; }
.s19 .ta-num { color:var(--amber); }
.s19 .ta-item h4 { font-size:23px; }
.s19 .ta-item p  { font-size:19px; }
</style>

<script>
/**
 * <deck-stage> — reusable web component for HTML decks.
 *
 * Handles:
 *  (a) speaker notes — reads <script type="application/json" id="speaker-notes">
 *      and posts {slideIndexChanged: N} to the parent window on nav.
 *  (b) keyboard navigation — ←/→, PgUp/PgDn, Space, Home/End, number keys.
 *  (c) press R to reset to slide 0 (with a tasteful keyboard hint).
 *  (d) bottom-center overlay showing slide count + hints, fades out on idle.
 *  (e) auto-scaling — inner canvas is a fixed design size (default 1920×1080)
 *      scaled with `transform: scale()` to fit the viewport, letterboxed.
 *      Set the `noscale` attribute to render at authored size (1:1) — the
 *      PPTX exporter sets this so its DOM capture sees unscaled geometry.
 *  (f) print — `@media print` lays every slide out as its own page at the
 *      design size, so the browser's Print → Save as PDF produces a clean
 *      one-page-per-slide PDF with no extra setup.
 *
 * Slides are HIDDEN, not unmounted. Non-active slides stay in the DOM with
 * `visibility: hidden` + `opacity: 0`, so their state (videos, iframes,
 * form inputs, React trees) is preserved across navigation.
 *
 * Lifecycle event — the component dispatches a `slidechange` CustomEvent on
 * itself whenever the active slide changes (including the initial mount).
 * The event bubbles and composes out of shadow DOM, so you can listen on
 * the <deck-stage> element or on document:
 *
 *   document.querySelector('deck-stage').addEventListener('slidechange', (e) => {
 *     e.detail.index         // new 0-based index
 *     e.detail.previousIndex // previous index, or -1 on init
 *     e.detail.total         // total slide count
 *     e.detail.slide         // the new active slide element
 *     e.detail.previousSlide // the prior slide element, or null on init
 *     e.detail.reason        // 'init' | 'keyboard' | 'click' | 'tap' | 'api'
 *   });
 *
 * Persistence: current slide index is saved to localStorage keyed by the
 * document path, so refresh returns you to the same place.
 *
 * Usage:
 *   <deck-stage width="1920" height="1080">
 *     <section data-label="Title">...</section>
 *     <section data-label="Agenda">...</section>
 *   </deck-stage>
 *
 * Slides are the direct element children of <deck-stage>. Each slide is
 * automatically tagged with:
 *   - data-screen-label="NN Label"   (1-indexed, for comment flow)
 *   - data-om-validate="no_overflowing_text,no_overlapping_text,slide_sized_text"
 */

(() => {
  const DESIGN_W_DEFAULT = 1920;
  const DESIGN_H_DEFAULT = 1080;
  const STORAGE_PREFIX = 'deck-stage:slide:';
  const OVERLAY_HIDE_MS = 1800;
  const VALIDATE_ATTR = 'no_overflowing_text,no_overlapping_text,slide_sized_text';

  const pad2 = (n) => String(n).padStart(2, '0');

  const stylesheet = `
    :host {
      position: fixed;
      inset: 0;
      display: block;
      background: #000;
      color: #fff;
      font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Helvetica Neue", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;
      overflow: hidden;
    }

    .stage {
      position: absolute;
      inset: 0;
      display: flex;
      align-items: center;
      justify-content: center;
    }

    .canvas {
      position: relative;
      transform-origin: center center;
      flex-shrink: 0;
      background: #fff;
      will-change: transform;
    }

    /* Slides live in light DOM (via <slot>) so authored CSS still applies.
       We absolutely position each slotted child to stack them. */
    ::slotted(*) {
      position: absolute !important;
      inset: 0 !important;
      width: 100% !important;
      height: 100% !important;
      box-sizing: border-box !important;
      overflow: hidden;
      opacity: 0;
      pointer-events: none;
      visibility: hidden;
    }
    ::slotted([data-deck-active]) {
      opacity: 1;
      pointer-events: auto;
      visibility: visible;
    }

    /* Tap zones for mobile — back/forward thirds like Stories.
       Transparent, no visible UI, don't block the overlay. */
    .tapzones {
      position: fixed;
      inset: 0;
      display: flex;
      z-index: 2147482000;
      pointer-events: none;
    }
    .tapzone {
      flex: 1;
      pointer-events: auto;
      -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent;
    }
    /* Only activate tap zones on coarse pointers (touch devices). */
    @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) {
      .tapzones { display: none; }
    }

    .overlay {
      position: fixed;
      left: 50%;
      bottom: 22px;
      transform: translate(-50%, 6px) scale(0.92);
      filter: blur(6px);
      display: flex;
      align-items: center;
      gap: 4px;
      padding: 4px;
      background: #000;
      color: #fff;
      border-radius: 999px;
      font-size: 12px;
      font-feature-settings: "tnum" 1;
      letter-spacing: 0.01em;
      opacity: 0;
      pointer-events: none;
      transition: opacity 260ms ease, transform 260ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1), filter 260ms ease;
      transform-origin: center bottom;
      z-index: 2147483000;
      user-select: none;
    }
    .overlay[data-visible] {
      opacity: 1;
      pointer-events: auto;
      transform: translate(-50%, 0) scale(1);
      filter: blur(0);
    }

    .btn {
      appearance: none;
      -webkit-appearance: none;
      background: transparent;
      border: 0;
      margin: 0;
      padding: 0;
      color: inherit;
      font: inherit;
      cursor: default;
      display: inline-flex;
      align-items: center;
      justify-content: center;
      height: 28px;
      min-width: 28px;
      border-radius: 999px;
      color: rgba(255,255,255,0.72);
      transition: background 140ms ease, color 140ms ease;
      -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent;
    }
    .btn:hover { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.12); color: #fff; }
    .btn:active { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.18); }
    .btn:focus { outline: none; }
    .btn:focus-visible { outline: none; }
    .btn::-moz-focus-inner { border: 0; }
    .btn svg { width: 14px; height: 14px; display: block; }
    .btn.reset {
      font-size: 11px;
      font-weight: 500;
      letter-spacing: 0.02em;
      padding: 0 10px 0 12px;
      gap: 6px;
      color: rgba(255,255,255,0.72);
    }
    .btn.reset .kbd {
      display: inline-flex;
      align-items: center;
      justify-content: center;
      min-width: 16px;
      height: 16px;
      padding: 0 4px;
      font-family: ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace;
      font-size: 10px;
      line-height: 1;
      color: rgba(255,255,255,0.88);
      background: rgba(255,255,255,0.12);
      border-radius: 4px;
    }

    .count {
      font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
      color: #fff;
      font-weight: 500;
      padding: 0 8px;
      min-width: 42px;
      text-align: center;
      font-size: 12px;
    }
    .count .sep { color: rgba(255,255,255,0.45); margin: 0 3px; font-weight: 400; }
    .count .total { color: rgba(255,255,255,0.55); }

    .divider {
      width: 1px;
      height: 14px;
      background: rgba(255,255,255,0.18);
      margin: 0 2px;
    }

    /* ── Print: one page per slide, no chrome ────────────────────────────
       The screen layout stacks every slide at inset:0 inside a scaled
       canvas; for print we want them in document flow at the authored
       design size so the browser paginates one slide per sheet. The
       @page size is set from the width/height attributes via the inline
       <style id="deck-stage-print-page"> that connectedCallback injects
       into <head> (the @page at-rule has no effect inside shadow DOM). */
    @media print {
      :host {
        position: static;
        inset: auto;
        background: none;
        overflow: visible;
        color: inherit;
      }
      .stage { position: static; display: block; }
      .canvas {
        transform: none !important;
        width: auto !important;
        height: auto !important;
        background: none;
        will-change: auto;
      }
      ::slotted(*) {
        position: relative !important;
        inset: auto !important;
        width: var(--deck-design-w) !important;
        height: var(--deck-design-h) !important;
        box-sizing: border-box !important;
        opacity: 1 !important;
        visibility: visible !important;
        pointer-events: auto;
        break-after: page;
        page-break-after: always;
        break-inside: avoid;
        overflow: hidden;
      }
      ::slotted(*:last-child) {
        break-after: auto;
        page-break-after: auto;
      }
      .overlay, .tapzones { display: none !important; }
    }
  `;

  class DeckStage extends HTMLElement {
    static get observedAttributes() { return ['width', 'height', 'noscale']; }

    constructor() {
      super();
      this._root = this.attachShadow({ mode: 'open' });
      this._index = 0;
      this._slides = [];
      this._notes = [];
      this._hideTimer = null;
      this._mouseIdleTimer = null;
      this._storageKey = STORAGE_PREFIX + (location.pathname || '/');

      this._onKey = this._onKey.bind(this);
      this._onResize = this._onResize.bind(this);
      this._onSlotChange = this._onSlotChange.bind(this);
      this._onMouseMove = this._onMouseMove.bind(this);
      this._onTapBack = this._onTapBack.bind(this);
      this._onTapForward = this._onTapForward.bind(this);
    }

    get designWidth() {
      return parseInt(this.getAttribute('width'), 10) || DESIGN_W_DEFAULT;
    }
    get designHeight() {
      return parseInt(this.getAttribute('height'), 10) || DESIGN_H_DEFAULT;
    }

    connectedCallback() {
      this._render();
      this._loadNotes();
      this._syncPrintPageRule();
      window.addEventListener('keydown', this._onKey);
      window.addEventListener('resize', this._onResize);
      window.addEventListener('mousemove', this._onMouseMove, { passive: true });
      // Initial collection + layout happens via slotchange, which fires on mount.
    }

    disconnectedCallback() {
      window.removeEventListener('keydown', this._onKey);
      window.removeEventListener('resize', this._onResize);
      window.removeEventListener('mousemove', this._onMouseMove);
      if (this._hideTimer) clearTimeout(this._hideTimer);
      if (this._mouseIdleTimer) clearTimeout(this._mouseIdleTimer);
    }

    attributeChangedCallback() {
      if (this._canvas) {
        this._canvas.style.width = this.designWidth + 'px';
        this._canvas.style.height = this.designHeight + 'px';
        this._canvas.style.setProperty('--deck-design-w', this.designWidth + 'px');
        this._canvas.style.setProperty('--deck-design-h', this.designHeight + 'px');
        this._fit();
        this._syncPrintPageRule();
      }
    }

    _render() {
      const style = document.createElement('style');
      style.textContent = stylesheet;

      const stage = document.createElement('div');
      stage.className = 'stage';

      const canvas = document.createElement('div');
      canvas.className = 'canvas';
      canvas.style.width = this.designWidth + 'px';
      canvas.style.height = this.designHeight + 'px';
      canvas.style.setProperty('--deck-design-w', this.designWidth + 'px');
      canvas.style.setProperty('--deck-design-h', this.designHeight + 'px');

      const slot = document.createElement('slot');
      slot.addEventListener('slotchange', this._onSlotChange);
      canvas.appendChild(slot);
      stage.appendChild(canvas);

      // Tap zones (mobile): left third = back, right third = forward.
      const tapzones = document.createElement('div');
      tapzones.className = 'tapzones export-hidden';
      tapzones.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
      const tzBack = document.createElement('div');
      tzBack.className = 'tapzone tapzone--back';
      const tzMid = document.createElement('div');
      tzMid.className = 'tapzone tapzone--mid';
      tzMid.style.pointerEvents = 'none';
      const tzFwd = document.createElement('div');
      tzFwd.className = 'tapzone tapzone--fwd';
      tzBack.addEventListener('click', this._onTapBack);
      tzFwd.addEventListener('click', this._onTapForward);
      tapzones.append(tzBack, tzMid, tzFwd);

      // Overlay: compact, solid black, with clickable controls.
      const overlay = document.createElement('div');
      overlay.className = 'overlay export-hidden';
      overlay.setAttribute('role', 'toolbar');
      overlay.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Deck controls');
      overlay.innerHTML = `
        <button class="btn prev" type="button" aria-label="Previous slide" title="Previous (←)">
          <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M10 3L5 8l5 5"/></svg>
        </button>
        <span class="count" aria-live="polite"><span class="current">1</span><span class="sep">/</span><span class="total">1</span></span>
        <button class="btn next" type="button" aria-label="Next slide" title="Next (→)">
          <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M6 3l5 5-5 5"/></svg>
        </button>
        <span class="divider"></span>
        <button class="btn reset" type="button" aria-label="Reset to first slide" title="Reset (R)">Reset<span class="kbd">R</span></button>
      `;

      overlay.querySelector('.prev').addEventListener('click', () => this._go(this._index - 1, 'click'));
      overlay.querySelector('.next').addEventListener('click', () => this._go(this._index + 1, 'click'));
      overlay.querySelector('.reset').addEventListener('click', () => this._go(0, 'click'));

      this._root.append(style, stage, tapzones, overlay);
      this._canvas = canvas;
      this._slot = slot;
      this._overlay = overlay;
      this._countEl = overlay.querySelector('.current');
      this._totalEl = overlay.querySelector('.total');
    }

    /** @page must live in the document stylesheet — it's a no-op inside
     *  shadow DOM. Inject/update a single <head> style tag so the print
     *  sheet matches the design size and Save-as-PDF yields one slide per
     *  page with no margins. */
    _syncPrintPageRule() {
      const id = 'deck-stage-print-page';
      let tag = document.getElementById(id);
      if (!tag) {
        tag = document.createElement('style');
        tag.id = id;
        document.head.appendChild(tag);
      }
      tag.textContent =
        '@page { size: ' + this.designWidth + 'px ' + this.designHeight + 'px; margin: 0; } ' +
        '@media print { html, body { margin: 0 !important; padding: 0 !important; background: none !important; overflow: visible !important; height: auto !important; } ' +
        '* { -webkit-print-color-adjust: exact; print-color-adjust: exact; } }';
    }

    _onSlotChange() {
      this._collectSlides();
      this._restoreIndex();
      this._applyIndex({ showOverlay: false, broadcast: true, reason: 'init' });
      this._fit();
    }

    _collectSlides() {
      const assigned = this._slot.assignedElements({ flatten: true });
      this._slides = assigned.filter((el) => {
        // Skip template/style/script nodes even if someone slots them.
        const tag = el.tagName;
        return tag !== 'TEMPLATE' && tag !== 'SCRIPT' && tag !== 'STYLE';
      });

      this._slides.forEach((slide, i) => {
        const n = i + 1;
        // Determine a label for comment flow: prefer explicit data-label,
        // then an existing data-screen-label, then first heading, else "Slide".
        let label = slide.getAttribute('data-label');
        if (!label) {
          const existing = slide.getAttribute('data-screen-label');
          if (existing) {
            // Strip any leading number the author may have included.
            label = existing.replace(/^\s*\d+\s*/, '').trim() || existing;
          }
        }
        if (!label) {
          const h = slide.querySelector('h1, h2, h3, [data-title]');
          if (h) label = (h.textContent || '').trim().slice(0, 40);
        }
        if (!label) label = 'Slide';
        slide.setAttribute('data-screen-label', `${pad2(n)} ${label}`);

        // Validation attribute for comment flow / auto-checks.
        if (!slide.hasAttribute('data-om-validate')) {
          slide.setAttribute('data-om-validate', VALIDATE_ATTR);
        }

        slide.setAttribute('data-deck-slide', String(i));
      });

      if (this._totalEl) this._totalEl.textContent = String(this._slides.length || 1);
      if (this._index >= this._slides.length) this._index = Math.max(0, this._slides.length - 1);
    }

    _loadNotes() {
      const tag = document.getElementById('speaker-notes');
      if (!tag) { this._notes = []; return; }
      try {
        const parsed = JSON.parse(tag.textContent || '[]');
        if (Array.isArray(parsed)) this._notes = parsed;
      } catch (e) {
        console.warn('[deck-stage] Failed to parse #speaker-notes JSON:', e);
        this._notes = [];
      }
    }

    _restoreIndex() {
      try {
        const raw = localStorage.getItem(this._storageKey);
        if (raw != null) {
          const n = parseInt(raw, 10);
          if (Number.isFinite(n) && n >= 0 && n < this._slides.length) {
            this._index = n;
          }
        }
      } catch (e) { /* ignore */ }
    }

    _persistIndex() {
      try { localStorage.setItem(this._storageKey, String(this._index)); }
      catch (e) { /* ignore */ }
    }

    _applyIndex({ showOverlay = true, broadcast = true, reason = 'init' } = {}) {
      if (!this._slides.length) return;
      const prev = this._prevIndex == null ? -1 : this._prevIndex;
      const curr = this._index;
      this._slides.forEach((s, i) => {
        if (i === curr) s.setAttribute('data-deck-active', '');
        else s.removeAttribute('data-deck-active');
      });
      if (this._countEl) this._countEl.textContent = String(curr + 1);
      this._persistIndex();

      if (broadcast) {
        // (1) Legacy: host-window postMessage for speaker-notes renderers.
        try { window.postMessage({ slideIndexChanged: curr }, '*'); } catch (e) {}

        // (2) In-page CustomEvent on the <deck-stage> element itself.
        //     Bubbles and composes out of shadow DOM so slide code can listen:
        //       document.querySelector('deck-stage').addEventListener('slidechange', e => {
        //         e.detail.index, e.detail.previousIndex, e.detail.total, e.detail.slide, e.detail.reason
        //       });
        const detail = {
          index: curr,
          previousIndex: prev,
          total: this._slides.length,
          slide: this._slides[curr] || null,
          previousSlide: prev >= 0 ? (this._slides[prev] || null) : null,
          reason: reason, // 'init' | 'keyboard' | 'click' | 'tap' | 'api'
        };
        this.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('slidechange', {
          detail,
          bubbles: true,
          composed: true,
        }));
      }

      this._prevIndex = curr;
      if (showOverlay) this._flashOverlay();
    }

    _flashOverlay() {
      if (!this._overlay) return;
      this._overlay.setAttribute('data-visible', '');
      if (this._hideTimer) clearTimeout(this._hideTimer);
      this._hideTimer = setTimeout(() => {
        this._overlay.removeAttribute('data-visible');
      }, OVERLAY_HIDE_MS);
    }

    _fit() {
      if (!this._canvas) return;
      // PPTX export sets noscale so the DOM capture sees authored-size
      // geometry — the scaled canvas is in shadow DOM, so the exporter's
      // resetTransformSelector can't reach .canvas.style.transform directly.
      if (this.hasAttribute('noscale')) {
        this._canvas.style.transform = 'none';
        return;
      }
      const vw = window.innerWidth;
      const vh = window.innerHeight;
      const s = Math.min(vw / this.designWidth, vh / this.designHeight);
      this._canvas.style.transform = `scale(${s})`;
    }

    _onResize() { this._fit(); }

    _onMouseMove() {
      // Keep overlay visible while mouse moves; hide after idle.
      this._flashOverlay();
    }

    _onTapBack(e) {
      e.preventDefault();
      this._go(this._index - 1, 'tap');
    }

    _onTapForward(e) {
      e.preventDefault();
      this._go(this._index + 1, 'tap');
    }

    _onKey(e) {
      // Ignore when the user is typing.
      const t = e.target;
      if (t && (t.isContentEditable || /^(INPUT|TEXTAREA|SELECT)$/.test(t.tagName))) return;
      if (e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey || e.altKey) return;

      const key = e.key;
      let handled = true;

      if (key === 'ArrowRight' || key === 'PageDown' || key === ' ' || key === 'Spacebar') {
        this._go(this._index + 1, 'keyboard');
      } else if (key === 'ArrowLeft' || key === 'PageUp') {
        this._go(this._index - 1, 'keyboard');
      } else if (key === 'Home') {
        this._go(0, 'keyboard');
      } else if (key === 'End') {
        this._go(this._slides.length - 1, 'keyboard');
      } else if (key === 'r' || key === 'R') {
        this._go(0, 'keyboard');
      } else if (/^[0-9]$/.test(key)) {
        // 1..9 jump to that slide; 0 jumps to 10.
        const n = key === '0' ? 9 : parseInt(key, 10) - 1;
        if (n < this._slides.length) this._go(n, 'keyboard');
      } else {
        handled = false;
      }

      if (handled) {
        e.preventDefault();
        this._flashOverlay();
      }
    }

    _go(i, reason = 'api') {
      if (!this._slides.length) return;
      const clamped = Math.max(0, Math.min(this._slides.length - 1, i));
      if (clamped === this._index) {
        this._flashOverlay();
        return;
      }
      this._index = clamped;
      this._applyIndex({ showOverlay: true, broadcast: true, reason });
    }

    // Public API ------------------------------------------------------------

    /** Current slide index (0-based). */
    get index() { return this._index; }
    /** Total slide count. */
    get length() { return this._slides.length; }
    /** Programmatically navigate. */
    goTo(i) { this._go(i, 'api'); }
    next() { this._go(this._index + 1, 'api'); }
    prev() { this._go(this._index - 1, 'api'); }
    reset() { this._go(0, 'api'); }
  }

  if (!customElements.get('deck-stage')) {
    customElements.define('deck-stage', DeckStage);
  }
})();

</script>
<script type="application/json" id="speaker-notes">
[
  "Welcome everyone. Today we're going to get under the hood of ActivitySim, specifically the initialization and accessibility components. These are the very first things that run when you kick off a model, and understanding them is foundational to everything that comes after. Whether you're debugging a run or customizing ActivitySim for your region, this is where it all begins.",

  "Let's start with some context for those of you coming from the 4-step world. In the 4-step model, we think of travel as aggregate flows — zone to zone, period to period. ActivitySim flips this. Instead of flows, we simulate individual people making decisions throughout their day. Each synthetic person has a household, a set of possible activities, and a travel pattern. This shift from aggregate to disaggregate is the core conceptual leap.",

  "Here's the full ActivitySim pipeline at a glance. Don't worry about memorizing all the components — the key thing to notice is the structure. There's a startup phase where data is loaded and checked. Then a brief aggregate phase — this is where accessibility is computed. Then a long disaggregate phase where every behavioral model runs, person by person. Today we're focused on everything before that disaggregate phase begins.",

  "So what does initialization actually do? It's not really a model in the behavioral sense — it doesn't predict anything. Think of it as the setup crew before the main event. There are four distinct steps: loading land use data, loading and annotating household and person records, loading network level-of-service data — the skims — and pre-loading tour structures. Each of these prepares the data pipeline for the behavioral models downstream.",

  "Initialize Land Use is the very first step. It reads your zonal land use file — things like total employment, retail employment, population — and registers it as a named table in the pipeline. One important thing: ActivitySim uses lazy loading, so the table isn't actually read until something needs it. But by registering it here, we ensure consistent random seed behavior throughout the run.",

  "Now let's talk about the inject system, which is the machinery behind Initialize Households. ActivitySim uses a dependency injection pattern. When initialize_households runs, it asks for the persons table. The persons table requires the households table. The households table reads from your CSV input. This chain of dependencies is resolved automatically — you declare what you need, and the system figures out the order. This lazy loading approach also enables the model to be resumed mid-run after a crash.",

  "Initialize LOS handles your skims — the level-of-service matrices that encode travel times and costs between zones. Depending on your zone system, this varies considerably. In a one-zone TAZ model, you load highway and transit skim OMX files. In a two-zone system, you also load MAZ-to-MAZ walk and bike tables. The three-zone system adds TAP-to-TAP transit skims and the Transit Virtual Path Builder, which pre-computes transit path utilities. The TVPB step can be computationally expensive, so caching is available.",

  "Initialize Tours is a lighter step. For implementations that pre-define tour structures — such as mandatory work and school tours — this step reads those records into the pipeline before the behavioral models start allocating time windows and scheduling. It ensures that the tour table exists with the right structure so downstream models can annotate it consistently.",

  "The Input Checker is an optional but highly recommended step that runs before everything else. It uses the Pandera library to validate your input data against user-defined rules. You write Python code that checks column types, value ranges, referential integrity — whatever matters for your implementation. If any check fails, ActivitySim stops immediately with a clear log message rather than crashing mysteriously later. Think of it as your data contract.",

  "Now let's shift to Accessibility. This is a concept most of you know from the 4-step world, but in ActivitySim it's made explicit as a pre-computed zonal measure. The question accessibility answers is: from this zone, how easy is it to reach employment opportunities? The answer depends on how much employment exists nearby, and how difficult it is to reach — measured by travel time decay. Zones with lots of nearby jobs are highly accessible; zones surrounded by only distant jobs are not.",

  "Here's the math. For each origin zone i, accessibility is the log-sum of employment at each destination j, weighted by a decay function of travel time. The decay function is exponential — jobs that are farther away contribute less to accessibility. Walk access uses a very steep decay, meaning only very close jobs count. Auto access uses a shallower decay. Three time periods are used: AM peak, midday, and PM peak. The logarithm at the end compresses the distribution so that very high employment concentrations don't dominate.",

  "Let's look at the inputs and outputs concretely. Inputs: highway skims for three time periods with drive-alone toll time, transit skims with in-vehicle time, wait times, and walk access/egress, and your land use file with total and retail employment. Outputs: ten accessibility measures per zone — auto and transit for peak and off-peak, non-motorized, each split between retail and total employment. These become columns in your accessibility table, one row per TAZ.",

  "Here's the critical insight about where accessibility sits in the pipeline. It runs immediately after Initialize Land Use — before households and persons are even loaded. This is intentional. Accessibility is an aggregate, zone-level calculation. It doesn't need person records. Once computed, these ten measures are attached to the land use table and become available as explanatory variables in the behavioral models: school location choice, work location choice, destination choice for non-mandatory tours. Accessibility is a bridge between the network and individual decision-making.",

  "Let me summarize what we've covered. Initialization is the data pipeline setup — four steps that load, validate, and annotate your inputs before any behavior is modeled. The inject system enables lazy loading and makes the pipeline restartable. Accessibility is an aggregate, zone-level calculation that sits at the boundary between network data and behavioral modeling — it translates travel time skims into a measure that individuals can respond to. In our next session we'll start looking at the behavioral models that consume these outputs. Questions?",

  "Now let's go deeper on a question that trips up even experienced modelers: what number actually gets used when a submodel like auto ownership needs to represent accessibility? In a 4-step model, each submodel picks its own shortcut — the gravity model uses raw travel time, auto ownership uses time-savings-over-transit, mode choice uses IVT. These ad hoc measures were chosen because they fit the observed data well — not because they're theoretically consistent with each other. ActivitySim faces the same choice: you can feed auto ownership an aggregate zone-level measure, or you can use a disaggregate logsum derived from the mode choice model. The choice has major consequences when a policy changes time and cost in opposite directions.",

  "Here's the canonical example from WFRC — the Wasatch Front Regional Council in Salt Lake City. They test a downtown cordon toll. The toll makes driving into downtown faster because it reduces congestion — but it also costs money. The auto ownership model uses ad hoc accessibility: auto time savings versus transit. When you run the model, it sees the time saving and predicts more people will own cars. But that's wrong — a toll should be a deterrent. The model never sees the cost because cost was never included in the accessibility measure. Use the sliders to explore this — set both toll cost and time saving, and watch what the ad hoc model predicts. Then set toll cost only, with no time saving, and see how the model goes silent on the cost entirely.",

  "The logsum is the theoretically consistent alternative. It falls directly out of the mathematics of your mode choice model — you don't add anything new. If your mode choice utility for driving is beta-time times travel time plus beta-cost times travel cost, then the logsum is just the log of the sum of exponentiated utilities across all modes. Cost is already in there. When you add a toll, V-auto drops, the logsum drops, and the auto ownership model predicts less car ownership — all automatically, all from one consistent specification. Use the calculator on the right to explore: add a cordon toll and watch V-auto and the logsum respond. Notice how transit becomes relatively more attractive as auto cost rises.",

  "Now the honest part — and this is what separates good modeling presentations from great ones. The pros of disaggregate accessibility are real: consistent policy responses, automatic improvement as mode choice improves, and a rigorous consumer surplus measure for benefit-cost analysis. But the cons are equally real. First, computing logsums per person is expensive. Second — and this is critical — adding the disaggregate step is only half the job. You then have to retrofit every submodel that currently uses an ad hoc measure. That's expensive and tedious. And third, the most uncomfortable truth: ad hoc measures like time savings may simply predict car ownership better than the logsum does. Theoretical elegance does not guarantee better fit. Strategy A and Strategy B are both legitimate — the choice depends on your policy environment and team capacity.",

  "To wrap up: we've covered the full initialization pipeline and now a deep dive on the three types of accessibility measures. Aggregate accessibility is the log-sum-of-employment pre-computed per zone — fast, simple, and feeds long-term decisions. Disaggregate accessibility uses mode choice logsums per person — consistent and theoretically sound, but expensive and hard to retrofit. Ad hoc measures are the pragmatic middle ground — chosen for fit, not consistency, but vulnerable to novel policies like cordon tolls. Understanding where each type is used in your model — and where it might break — is foundational knowledge for any ActivitySim practitioner."
]
</script>

<!-- ════════ SLIDE 1 — TITLE ════════ -->
<section class="s1" data-label="Title">
  <div class="eyebrow an fi d0">ActivitySim Deep Dive · Session 2</div>
  <h1 class="an fu d1">Initialization<br>&amp; <em>Accessibility</em></h1>
  <div class="subtitle an fu d2">How ActivitySim loads data, validates inputs, and<br>computes the first aggregate measure of the model run.</div>
  <div class="meta an fi d3">
    <div class="meta-chip">Audience: <span>Travel Demand Modelers</span></div>
    <div class="meta-dot"></div>
    <div class="meta-chip">Focus: <span>Initialization Components &amp; Accessibility Model</span></div>
    <div class="meta-dot"></div>
    <div class="meta-chip">Reference: <span>ActivitySim v1.5.1</span></div>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- ════════ SLIDE 2 — 4-STEP vs ABM ════════ -->
<section class="s2" data-label="From 4-Step to Activity-Based Modeling">
  <div class="eyebrow an fi d0">Context</div>
  <div class="slide-title an fu d1">From 4-Step to Activity-Based Modeling</div>
  <div class="compare-grid">
    <div class="compare-col an si d2">
      <div class="tag teal">4-Step Model</div>
      <h3>Aggregate Flows</h3>
      <div class="compare-item"><div class="ci-bullet"></div><p>Trip generation: zone-level productions &amp; attractions</p></div>
      <div class="compare-item"><div class="ci-bullet"></div><p>Trip distribution: gravity model, zone-to-zone OD matrices</p></div>
      <div class="compare-item"><div class="ci-bullet"></div><p>Mode choice: logit on aggregate OD pairs</p></div>
      <div class="compare-item"><div class="ci-bullet"></div><p>Traffic assignment: flows on network links</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="compare-arrow an fi d3">→</div>
    <div class="compare-col dark an si d2">
      <div class="tag navy">Activity-Based Model</div>
      <h3>Synthetic Individuals</h3>
      <div class="compare-item"><div class="ci-bullet"></div><p>Each person has a daily activity pattern, not a trip list</p></div>
      <div class="compare-item"><div class="ci-bullet"></div><p>Tours link outbound + return trips around a primary activity</p></div>
      <div class="compare-item"><div class="ci-bullet"></div><p>Choices are sequential and interdependent per person</p></div>
      <div class="compare-item"><div class="ci-bullet"></div><p>Time of day, destination, mode decided together</p></div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="compare-note an fu d4">
    <strong>Key shift:</strong> ActivitySim simulates <em>individuals</em>, not zone-level flows — but it still needs aggregate zone data (skims, land use, accessibility) as inputs to individual decisions.
  </div>
</section>

<!-- ════════ SLIDE 4 — INIT OVERVIEW ════════ -->
<section class="s4" data-label="Initialization: Four Data Processing Steps">
  <div class="eyebrow an fi d0">Initialization</div>
  <div class="slide-title an fu d1">Four Data Processing Steps</div>
  <div class="init-grid">
    <div class="init-card an si d2">
      <div class="ic-num">1</div>
      <div>
        <h3>Initialize Land Use</h3>
        <p>Registers zonal employment and demographic data in the pipeline. First table loaded — sets the spatial foundation.</p>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="init-card an si d3">
      <div class="ic-num">2</div>
      <div>
        <h3>Initialize Households &amp; Persons</h3>
        <p>Lazy-loads household and person records. Annotates tables with derived variables like value-of-time. Resolves dependency chain via the inject system.</p>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="init-card amber an si d4">
      <div class="ic-num amber">3</div>
      <div>
        <h3>Initialize LOS</h3>
        <p>Loads highway and transit skims from OMX files. In three-zone systems, pre-computes Transit Virtual Path Builder (TVPB) utilities and caches them.</p>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="init-card amber an si d5">
      <div class="ic-num amber">4</div>
      <div>
        <h3>Initialize Tours</h3>
        <p>Pre-loads tour structures for implementations that define mandatory tours before behavioral models run. Ensures the tour table exists for downstream annotation.</p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="init-note an fu d6">
    <strong>Important:</strong> None of these steps predict behavior. They are <strong>data pipeline steps</strong> — loading, annotating, and registering data for the behavioral models that follow.
  </div>
</section>

<!-- ════════ SLIDE 5 — LAND USE ════════ -->
<section class="s5" data-label="Step 1 — Initialize Land Use">
  <div class="left">
    <div class="eyebrow an fi d0">Step 1</div>
    <div class="slide-title an fu d1">Initialize Land Use</div>
    <p class="body-text an fu d2">
      The land use table contains <strong>zonal attributes</strong> — employment counts, population, and other socioeconomic data indexed by zone ID. It is the first table loaded because nearly everything depends on it.
    </p>
    <p class="body-text an fu d3" style="margin-bottom:0;">
      The <strong>inject system</strong> registers it lazily: it is not read from disk until first requested. Once loaded, it is cached in the pipeline for all downstream models.
    </p>
    <div class="yaml-block an fu d4" style="margin-top:24px; font-size:17px;">
      <span class="yc"># settings.yaml — table registration</span><br>
      <span class="yk">input_table_list</span>:<br>
      &nbsp; - <span class="yk">tablename</span>: <span class="yv">land_use</span><br>
      &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<span class="yk">filename</span>: <span class="yv">land_use.csv</span><br>
      &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<span class="yk">index_col</span>: <span class="yv">zone_id</span><br>
      &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<span class="yk">column_map</span>:<br>
      &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<span class="yk">ZONE</span>: <span class="yv">zone_id</span>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="right an si d3">
    <div class="dt">
      <div class="dt-head">
        <span>zone_id</span><span>TOTEMP</span><span>RETEMPN</span><span>TOTPOP</span>
      </div>
      <div class="dt-row"><span class="zone">1001</span><span class="val">14,820</span><span class="val">2,140</span><span class="val">8,320</span></div>
      <div class="dt-row"><span class="zone">1002</span><span class="val">6,350</span><span class="val">890</span><span class="val">12,150</span></div>
      <div class="dt-row"><span class="zone">1003</span><span class="val">1,200</span><span class="val">340</span><span class="val">22,400</span></div>
      <div class="dt-row"><span class="zone">1004</span><span class="val">38,600</span><span class="val">5,800</span><span class="val">3,100</span></div>
      <div class="dt-row"><span class="zone">1005</span><span class="val">780</span><span class="val">120</span><span class="val">19,200</span></div>
    </div>
    <div style="background:#fff; border-radius:12px; padding:24px 28px; box-shadow:0 2px 14px rgba(0,0,0,0.06);">
      <div style="font-size:16px; font-weight:700; letter-spacing:0.08em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--navy); margin-bottom:12px;">Key Columns Used by Accessibility</div>
      <div style="display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:10px;">
        <div style="display:flex; gap:12px; align-items:center; font-size:20px;">
          <span style="font-family:var(--mono); background:var(--teal-lt); color:var(--teal); padding:2px 10px; border-radius:6px; font-weight:600;">TOTEMP</span>
          <span style="color:var(--muted);">Total employment</span>
        </div>
        <div style="display:flex; gap:12px; align-items:center; font-size:20px;">
          <span style="font-family:var(--mono); background:var(--teal-lt); color:var(--teal); padding:2px 10px; border-radius:6px; font-weight:600;">RETEMPN</span>
          <span style="color:var(--muted);">Retail trade employment</span>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- ════════ SLIDE 6 — INJECT SYSTEM ════════ -->
<section class="s6" data-label="Step 2 — Initialize Households and Persons">
  <div class="left">
    <div class="eyebrow an fi d0">Step 2</div>
    <div class="slide-title an fu d1" style="font-size:58px;">Initialize Households &amp; Persons</div>
    <p class="body-text an fu d2">
      ActivitySim uses <strong>dependency injection</strong> — each model declares what data it needs, and the framework resolves dependencies automatically.
    </p>
    <p class="body-text an fu d3">
      When <code style="font-family:var(--mono); background:var(--teal-lt); color:var(--teal); padding:2px 8px; border-radius:4px;">initialize_households</code> runs, it triggers a chain of lazy loads, annotates the tables with derived variables, and registers them in the pipeline.
    </p>
    <div class="an fu d4" style="background:var(--amber-lt); border-left:4px solid var(--amber); border-radius:10px; padding:18px 22px; font-size:21px; line-height:1.5; color:var(--navy);">
      <strong>Restartability:</strong> Because tables are loaded on-demand and checkpointed, a failed run can resume from any completed step — not restart from scratch.
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="right">
    <div class="inject-bg an si d2">
      <div style="font-size:15px; font-weight:700; letter-spacing:0.1em; text-transform:uppercase; color:rgba(255,255,255,0.4); margin-bottom:18px; padding-bottom:12px; border-bottom:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.1);">Dependency Resolution Chain</div>
      <div class="inject-tree">
        <div class="it-row an fu d3">
          <div class="it-box root">initialize_households()</div>
          <span class="it-label lt">STEP</span>
        </div>
        <div class="it-row an fu d4">
          <div class="it-indent" style="width:28px;"></div>
          <div style="color:rgba(255,255,255,0.2); margin-right:8px; font-size:20px;">├─</div>
          <div class="it-box dep1">needs: <strong style="color:oklch(0.72 0.13 196);">persons</strong> table</div>
        </div>
        <div class="it-row an fu d5">
          <div class="it-indent" style="width:56px;"></div>
          <div style="color:rgba(255,255,255,0.2); margin-right:8px; font-size:20px;">├─</div>
          <div class="it-box dep2">needs: <strong style="color:rgba(255,255,255,0.7);">households</strong> table</div>
        </div>
        <div class="it-row an fu d6">
          <div class="it-indent" style="width:84px;"></div>
          <div style="color:rgba(255,255,255,0.2); margin-right:8px; font-size:20px;">└─</div>
          <div class="it-box leaf">read_input_table("households.csv")</div>
          <span class="it-label la">I/O</span>
        </div>
        <div class="it-row an fu d6">
          <div class="it-indent" style="width:56px;"></div>
          <div style="color:rgba(255,255,255,0.2); margin-right:8px; font-size:20px;">└─</div>
          <div class="it-box dep2">read_input_table("persons.csv")</div>
        </div>
        <div class="it-row an fu d7">
          <div class="it-indent" style="width:28px;"></div>
          <div style="color:rgba(255,255,255,0.2); margin-right:8px; font-size:20px;">├─</div>
          <div class="it-box dep1">needs: <strong style="color:oklch(0.72 0.13 196);">land_use</strong> table</div>
          <span class="it-label lt">cached</span>
        </div>
        <div class="it-row an fu d8">
          <div class="it-indent" style="width:28px;"></div>
          <div style="color:rgba(255,255,255,0.2); margin-right:8px; font-size:20px;">└─</div>
          <div class="it-box dep1">annotate tables, set up RNG channels</div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- ════════ SLIDE 7 — INIT LOS ════════ -->
<section class="s7" data-label="Step 3 — Initialize LOS">
  <div class="eyebrow amber an fi d0">Step 3</div>
  <div class="slide-title white an fu d1">Initialize LOS — Skims &amp; Network</div>
  <div class="los-grid">
    <div class="los-card an si d2">
      <h3 class="teal">One-Zone System (TAZ)</h3>
      <div class="los-item"><div class="li-dot"></div><p>Highway OMX skims: IVTT, distance, cost by time period (AM, MD, PM)</p></div>
      <div class="los-item"><div class="li-dot"></div><p>Transit OMX skims: IVT, initial wait, transfer wait, walk access/egress</p></div>
      <div class="los-item"><div class="li-dot"></div><p>All OD pairs at TAZ level</p></div>
      <div style="margin-top:auto;">
        <div style="font-size:15px; font-weight:600; letter-spacing:0.07em; text-transform:uppercase; color:rgba(255,255,255,0.35); margin-bottom:10px;">Skim matrix (TAZ × TAZ)</div>
        <div class="skim-mini" id="skim-grid"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="los-card an si d3">
      <h3 class="amber">Two-Zone System (MAZ + TAZ)</h3>
      <div class="los-item"><div class="li-dot amber"></div><p>All one-zone skims, plus MAZ-to-MAZ walk &amp; bike tables</p></div>
      <div class="los-item"><div class="li-dot amber"></div><p>Blended impedance near origins: MAZ→MAZ for short, TAZ→TAZ for longer</p></div>
      <div class="los-item"><div class="li-dot amber"></div><p>Origins/destinations at MAZ level; auto/transit at TAZ level</p></div>
      <div class="los-bottom">
        <strong>Example blend formula:</strong><br>
        <span style="font-family:var(--mono); font-size:16px; color:rgba(255,255,255,0.5);">MAZ_dist × (d/max_d) +<br>TAZ_dist × (1 − d/max_d)</span>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="los-card an si d4">
      <h3 class="white">Three-Zone System (MAZ + TAZ + TAP)</h3>
      <div class="los-item"><div class="li-dot" style="background:rgba(255,255,255,0.4);"></div><p>Adds TAP-to-TAP transit skims (boarding to alighting stop clusters)</p></div>
      <div class="los-item"><div class="li-dot" style="background:rgba(255,255,255,0.4);"></div><p>MAZ-to-TAP walk &amp; drive access/egress tables</p></div>
      <div class="los-item"><div class="li-dot" style="background:rgba(255,255,255,0.4);"></div><p><strong style="color:rgba(255,255,255,0.7);">TVPB</strong>: pre-computes all TAP→TAP path utilities by demographic segment &amp; time period. Cached for reuse.</p></div>
      <div style="margin-top:auto; padding:12px 16px; border-radius:8px; background:rgba(255,255,255,0.07); font-size:17px; color:rgba(255,255,255,0.45);">
        ⚠ Three-zone approach being deprecated — new implementations should use one- or two-zone.
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- ════════ SLIDE 8 — INIT TOURS ════════ -->
<section class="s8" data-label="Step 4 — Initialize Tours">
  <div class="left">
    <div class="eyebrow an fi d0">Step 4</div>
    <div class="slide-title an fu d1">Initialize Tours</div>
    <p class="body-text an fu d2">
      In ActivitySim, travel is organized as <strong>tours</strong> — not individual trips. A tour begins and ends at home, with a primary destination and optional intermediate stops.
    </p>
    <p class="body-text an fu d3">
      The Initialize Tours step pre-loads tour structures before behavioral models run. This ensures the tour table exists with the correct index and schema so downstream models can safely annotate and extend it.
    </p>
    <div class="yaml-block an fu d4" style="margin-top:4px; font-size:17px;">
      <span class="yc"># Example: mandatory tours pre-defined per person</span><br>
      <span class="yk">tour_id</span>: <span class="yv">10010001</span>&nbsp;&nbsp;<span class="yc"># person 1001, tour 1</span><br>
      <span class="yk">person_id</span>: <span class="yv">1001</span><br>
      <span class="yk">tour_type</span>: <span class="yv">work</span><br>
      <span class="yk">tour_num</span>: <span class="yv">1</span><br>
      <span class="yk">number_of_participants</span>: <span class="yv">1</span>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="right">
    <div class="tour-type an fu d2">
      <div class="tt-icon teal">W</div>
      <div>
        <h4>Mandatory — Work</h4>
        <p>Persons with work tours; departure, arrival, mode, and intermediate stops are all modeled</p>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="tour-type an fu d3">
      <div class="tt-icon teal">S</div>
      <div>
        <h4>Mandatory — School</h4>
        <p>Children and students; destination choice for school location feeds into these tours</p>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="tour-type an fu d4">
      <div class="tt-icon amber">N</div>
      <div>
        <h4>Non-Mandatory</h4>
        <p>Shopping, recreation, meals — generated later in the pipeline, not pre-initialized</p>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="tour-type an fu d5">
      <div class="tt-icon navy">J</div>
      <div>
        <h4>Joint</h4>
        <p>Household members traveling together; requires coordination across person records</p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- ════════ SLIDE 9 — INPUT CHECKER ════════ -->
<section class="s9" data-label="Input Checker — Data Quality Gate">
  <div class="left">
    <div class="eyebrow an fi d0">Optional — Runs First</div>
    <div class="slide-title an fu d1">Input Checker</div>
    <p class="body-text an fu d2">
      The Input Checker validates your input data <strong>before</strong> anything else runs. It uses the <strong>Pandera</strong> Python library — you write the checks, ActivitySim runs them.
    </p>
    <div class="checker-list an fu d3">
      <div class="checker-item">
        <div class="ci-num">1</div>
        <p>Copy <code style="font-family:var(--mono); background:var(--teal-lt); color:var(--teal); padding:1px 6px; border-radius:4px;">input_checks.py</code> and <code style="font-family:var(--mono); background:var(--teal-lt); color:var(--teal); padding:1px 6px; border-radius:4px;">enums.py</code> from example folder (prototype_mtc_extended)</p>
      </div>
      <div class="checker-item">
        <div class="ci-num">2</div>
        <p>Modify to match your data: column names, value ranges, referential integrity, categorical encodings</p>
      </div>
      <div class="checker-item">
        <div class="ci-num">3</div>
        <p>Add <code style="font-family:var(--mono); background:var(--teal-lt); color:var(--teal); padding:1px 6px; border-radius:4px;">input_checker</code> as the first model in <code style="font-family:var(--mono);">settings.yaml</code></p>
      </div>
      <div class="checker-item">
        <div class="ci-num">4</div>
        <p>Checks can be <strong>errors</strong> (fatal) or <strong>warnings</strong> (logged but continue)</p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="right an si d2">
    <div class="flow-diagram">
      <div class="fd-box input">Input Data<br><span style="font-size:16px; font-weight:400; opacity:0.7;">households.csv · persons.csv · land_use.csv · skims.omx</span></div>
      <div class="fd-arrow">↓</div>
      <div class="fd-box check">input_checker<br><span style="font-size:16px; font-weight:400; opacity:0.7;">Pandera validation · user-defined rules</span></div>
      <div class="fd-arrow">↓</div>
      <div class="fd-split">
        <div>
          <div class="fd-box pass">✓ All checks pass<br><span style="font-size:15px; font-weight:400;">Pipeline continues</span></div>
        </div>
        <div>
          <div class="fd-box fail">✗ Check fails<br><span style="font-size:15px; font-weight:400;">Crash → input_checker.log</span></div>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div style="background:var(--navy); color:rgba(255,255,255,0.6); border-radius:10px; padding:16px 20px; font-size:18px; line-height:1.5; font-family:var(--mono);">
        activitysim run -c configs -d data<br>
        &nbsp;&nbsp;-o output <span style="color:oklch(0.72 0.13 196);">--data_model data_model</span>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- ════════ SLIDE 10 — ACCESSIBILITY CONCEPT ════════ -->
<section class="s10" data-label="Accessibility — Concept and Purpose">
  <div class="eyebrow amber an fi d0">Part 2 of Today's Session</div>
  <div class="slide-title white an fu d1">Accessibility</div>
  <div class="big-def an fu d2">
    From any zone, how much employment can residents <em>realistically reach</em> — weighted by how hard it is to get there?
  </div>
  <div class="concept-pills an fi d3">
    <div class="concept-pill active">Origin-based</div>
    <div class="concept-pill active">Aggregate · zone-level</div>
    <div class="concept-pill active">Mode-specific</div>
    <div class="concept-pill active">Time-period sensitive</div>
    <div class="concept-pill">One row per TAZ</div>
    <div class="concept-pill">Pre-computed once</div>
  </div>
  <div class="vs-note an fu d4">
    In the 4-step model, accessibility is implicit in the gravity model's friction factors. <strong>ActivitySim makes it explicit:</strong> a pre-computed table of zonal measures that individual agents respond to in their location and destination choices.
  </div>
</section>

<!-- ════════ SLIDE 11 — FORMULA ════════ -->
<section class="s11" data-label="The Accessibility Calculation">
  <div class="left">
    <div class="eyebrow an fi d0">The Calculation</div>
    <div class="slide-title an fu d1" style="font-size:60px;">The Accessibility Formula</div>
    <div class="formula-box an si d2">
      <div class="f-label">Accessibility for origin zone i</div>
      <div class="f-main">
        <span class="fv">A</span><sub>i</sub> = ln&thinsp;(&thinsp; Σ<sub>j</sub> &thinsp;<span class="fk">Emp</span><sub>j</sub> &thinsp;× &thinsp;e<sup>−β·t<sub>ij</sub></sup> &thinsp;)
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="formula-parts">
      <div class="formula-part an fu d3">
        <span class="fp-key">Emp_j</span>
        <span class="fp-def">Employment at destination zone j (total or retail)</span>
      </div>
      <div class="formula-part an fu d4">
        <span class="fp-key amber">t_ij</span>
        <span class="fp-def">Round-trip travel time from i to j (mode &amp; period specific)</span>
      </div>
      <div class="formula-part an fu d5">
        <span class="fp-key">β</span>
        <span class="fp-def">Decay parameter — steeper for walk, shallower for auto</span>
      </div>
      <div class="formula-part an fu d6">
        <span class="fp-key amber">ln(·)</span>
        <span class="fp-def">Log-sum compresses distribution, prevents high-density zones from dominating</span>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="right">
    <div class="decay-card an si d2">
      <div class="dc-title">Decay Function by Mode</div>
      <canvas id="decayCanvas" width="580" height="280"></canvas>
      <div class="decay-legend">
        <div class="dl-item"><div class="dl-dot" style="background:#1b9aaa;"></div> Auto (shallow decay)</div>
        <div class="dl-item"><div class="dl-dot" style="background:#d4840a;"></div> Transit (medium)</div>
        <div class="dl-item"><div class="dl-dot" style="background:#5a6e80;"></div> Walk (steep decay)</div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div style="background:var(--navy); border-radius:12px; padding:22px 26px; an si d4">
      <div style="font-size:15px; font-weight:700; letter-spacing:0.08em; text-transform:uppercase; color:rgba(255,255,255,0.4); margin-bottom:12px;">Three Time Periods</div>
      <div style="display:flex; gap:12px;">
        <div style="flex:1; background:oklch(0.3 0.1 72/0.4); border:1px solid oklch(0.72 0.14 72/0.5); border-radius:8px; padding:12px 16px; text-align:center;">
          <div style="font-size:22px; font-weight:700; color:oklch(0.72 0.14 72);">AM</div>
          <div style="font-size:15px; color:rgba(255,255,255,0.5);">6am – 10am</div>
        </div>
        <div style="flex:1; background:oklch(0.3 0.1 196/0.3); border:1px solid var(--teal)/0.5; border-radius:8px; padding:12px 16px; text-align:center;">
          <div style="font-size:22px; font-weight:700; color:var(--teal);">MD</div>
          <div style="font-size:15px; color:rgba(255,255,255,0.5);">10am – 3pm</div>
        </div>
        <div style="flex:1; background:oklch(0.3 0.1 72/0.4); border:1px solid oklch(0.72 0.14 72/0.5); border-radius:8px; padding:12px 16px; text-align:center;">
          <div style="font-size:22px; font-weight:700; color:oklch(0.72 0.14 72);">PM</div>
          <div style="font-size:15px; color:rgba(255,255,255,0.5);">3pm – 7pm</div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
